- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Raml is a system of divination also known as "Arabic geomancy."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Raml is similar to African geomancy in that it uses symbols and figures to answer questions and provide guidance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There are key differences between African geomancy and Raml.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In African geomancy, there are 16 figures, while in Raml there are only 8.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The figures in Raml are different than the figures in African geomancy and have different meanings and interpretations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In African geomancy, the figures are created by casting a handful of soil or sand and interpreting the patterns that are formed.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In Raml, the figures are created by drawing lines in the sand or on paper.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The interpretation of the figures and the answers to the questions being asked are different between the two systems.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both African geomancy and Raml use symbols and figures to answer questions, but the interpretation of those symbols and figures is unique to each system.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, while African geomancy and Raml are similar in some ways, they are distinct and separate systems of divination with their own unique symbols, figures, methods, and interpretations.
